regimens.dose_text: 15 to 20 mg/kg IV every 8 to 12 hours (usual initial adult dose 1 g to 1.5 g IV every 12 hours). Administer by IV infusion over at least 60 minutes at a rate not exceeding 10 mg/min to prevent infusion-related reactions (red man syndrome). Therapeutic drug monitoring required: target AUC/MIC 400 to 600 or trough 15 to 20 mcg/mL.

value: Infusion-related reactions ('Red Man Syndrome'): flushing of upper body/neck, pruritus, erythema, urticaria, chills (rate-dependent; prevent by infusing <=10 mg/min or over >=60 min)
Injection site thrombophlebitis and local pain

refs.quote: Infusion-Related Events During or soon after rapid infusion of vancomycin hydrochloride for injection, patients may develop anaphylactoid reactions, including hypotension (see ANIMAL PHARMACOLOGY ), wheezing, dyspnea, urticaria, or pruritus.

value: Nephrotoxicity and Acute Kidney Injury (AKI; dose- and trough-dependent, significantly increased with AUC >600 mg*h/L, troughs >20 mcg/mL, or concomitant nephrotoxic agents like aminoglycosides, piperacillin-tazobactam, NSAIDs; monitor AUC/MIC or troughs)
Ototoxicity (sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus, vertigo; may be permanent; risk increased with high serum concentrations or concomitant ototoxic drugs)
Severe anaphylaxis and hypotension / cardiovascular collapse during rapid infusion
Severe cutaneous adverse reactions: DRESS syndrome, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, linear IgA bullous dermatosis
Neutropenia (reversible on cessation; periodic CBC monitoring for prolonged courses >1-2 weeks)

refs.quote: Nephrotoxicity Systemic vancomycin exposure may result in acute kidney injury (AKI). The risk of AKI increases as systemic exposure/serum levels increase.

value.drug_or_class: Nephrotoxic and Ototoxic Agents (Aminoglycosides, Amphotericin B, Polymyxin B, Cisplatin)
value.effect: Additive or synergistic nephrotoxicity and eighth-cranial-nerve ototoxicity with concurrent or sequential systemic administration.
value.management: Monitor renal function (serum creatinine, eGFR) and vancomycin trough concentrations frequently; avoid combinations when feasible.

refs.quote: Monitor renal function in patients receiving vancomycin and concurrent and/or sequential systemic or topical use of other potentially, neurotoxic and/or nephrotoxic drugs, such as amphotericin B, aminoglycosides, bacitracin, polymyxin B, colistin, viomycin, or cisplatin.

value.effect: Concomitant administration has been associated with erythema, histamine-like flushing, and anaphylactoid reactions.
value.management: Infuse vancomycin over at least 60 minutes prior to anesthetic induction to minimize histamine-mediated infusion reactions.

refs.quote: Concomitant administration of vancomycin and anesthetic agents has been associated with erythema and histamine-like flushing (see Pediatric Use, PRECAUTIONS ) and anaphylactoid reactions (see ADVERSE REACTIONS ).

renal_impairment.description: Dosage must be adjusted according to creatinine clearance in patients with renal impairment. Serum concentrations (troughs) must be monitored closely to optimize therapeutic efficacy and avoid nephrotoxicity.
